deck.name: English Core · A1–A2
deck.summary: The everyday words you need before anything else. Beginner to elementary.

senses.definition: inside something, or during a period of time

examples.text: The keys are in my bag.
My birthday is in May.

senses.usageNote: Use 'in' for months, years and seasons, 'on' for days and dates, and 'at' for clock times.

senses.definition: to own or keep something

examples.text: I have two cats.
She has a new phone.

senses.definition: to eat or drink something

examples.text: Let's have lunch.

senses.definition: used to say who gets something, why, or how long

examples.text: This present is for you.
I waited for an hour.

senses.usageNote: Use 'for' with a length of time (for two days) and 'since' with a starting point (since Monday).

senses.definition: touching the top of something; also used with days and dates

examples.text: Your book is on the table.
I'll see you on Monday.

senses.definition: together with someone or something

examples.text: I live with my parents.
Cut the paper with scissors.

senses.definition: to carry out an action or activity

examples.text: I do my homework after dinner.

senses.usageNote: We say 'do homework', 'do exercise' and 'do the shopping', but 'make a mistake' and 'make a cake'.

senses.definition: used to add something different or surprising

examples.text: It's small but very nice.

senses.usageNote: Do not use 'although' and 'but' together in one sentence, as you might in Chinese (虽然……但是).

senses.definition: used to show where something starts or where someone was born

examples.text: I'm from Shanghai.
The shop is open from nine to five.

translations.zh: 这家店从九点营业到五点。

senses.definition: used to say how you travel or do something

examples.text: We went there by train.

senses.definition: near or next to

examples.text: Sit by the window.

senses.definition: every one of a group, or the whole of something

examples.text: All the children are in the garden.

translations.zh: 所有的孩子都在花园里。

senses.usageNote: Say 'all the students' or 'all students', but not 'all of students'; 'of' needs 'the': 'all of the students'.

senses.definition: to be able to do something, or to be allowed to

examples.text: Can you swim?

senses.usageNote: After 'can' use the verb without 'to': 'I can swim', not 'I can to swim'.

senses.definition: to enjoy something or think someone is nice

examples.text: I like chocolate.

senses.usageNote: 'Would like' is a polite way to say 'want': 'I'd like a cup of tea.'

senses.definition: the same as or similar to

examples.text: She looks like her mother.

senses.definition: and for this reason

examples.text: It was raining, so we stayed inside.

translations.zh: 下雨了，所以我们待在屋里。

senses.usageNote: Don't use 'because' and 'so' together in one sentence, as you might with 因为……所以.

senses.definition: very; to a great degree

examples.text: I'm so happy to see you!

senses.definition: in or to that place

examples.text: Put the box over there.

senses.definition: used with 'be' to say that something exists

examples.text: There is a cat on the roof.

senses.usageNote: Don't say 'Have a cat on the roof' for 有; say 'There is a cat on the roof'.

senses.definition: to receive, buy or bring something

examples.text: Can you get some bread from the shop?

translations.zh: 你能从商店买点面包吗？

examples.text: I got a letter today.

senses.definition: to become

examples.text: It's getting cold.

senses.definition: used to say that one thing can happen only when another happens

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay inside.

translations.zh: 如果下雨，我们就待在屋里。

senses.usageNote: Don't use 'will' after 'if' for the future: 'If it rains', not 'If it will rain'.

senses.definition: to produce or build something

examples.text: Let's make a cake.
She made a card for her mum.
examples.cloze: She {{made}} a card for her mum.

translations.zh: 她给妈妈做了一张卡片。

senses.usageNote: Chinese learners often mix 'make' and 'do'. We 'make a mistake', 'make friends', but 'do homework', 'do sport'.

senses.definition: on the subject of something

examples.text: This book is about a little dog.

translations.zh: 这本书讲的是一只小狗。

senses.definition: a little more or less than a number

examples.text: It takes about ten minutes.

senses.definition: to move or travel from one place to another

examples.text: Let's go to the park.
We went home early.

senses.usageNote: Don't use 'to' before 'home': 'go home', not 'go to home'.

senses.definition: to speak words

examples.text: What did you say?
She said hello to everyone.

senses.usageNote: 'Say' is followed by the words: 'say sorry'. 'Tell' is followed by a person: 'tell me', not 'say me'.

senses.definition: used to ask at what time something happens

examples.text: When is your birthday?

senses.definition: at the time that

examples.text: Call me when you get home.

translations.zh: 你到家的时候给我打电话。

senses.definition: to have information in your mind, or to be familiar with a person or place

examples.text: I don't know the answer.
I've known her for years.

senses.usageNote: 'Know' is not usually used in the '-ing' form. Say 'I know', not 'I am knowing'.

senses.definition: a bigger number or amount

examples.text: Would you like some more rice?

senses.definition: used before adjectives to compare things

examples.text: This book is more interesting.

senses.definition: away from the inside of a place; not at home

examples.text: Let's go out for dinner.
Sorry, she's out at the moment.

senses.definition: a very short time ago

examples.text: I've just finished my lunch.

senses.definition: only; simply

examples.text: It's just a small cut.

senses.definition: to carry or bring something or someone with you

examples.text: Take an umbrella with you.

senses.definition: to need an amount of time

examples.text: It takes ten minutes to walk there.

senses.definition: what we measure in hours and minutes

examples.text: What time is it?
I don't have time to watch TV.

senses.definition: an occasion when something happens

examples.text: I've been to Paris three times.

senses.definition: towards a higher place or position

examples.text: Look up at the sky!

senses.definition: different or extra; not the one already talked about

examples.text: Where are the other children?
They help each other.

senses.usageNote: Use 'another' before a singular noun (another cake) and 'other' before plural nouns (other cakes).

senses.definition: in what way, or in what condition

examples.text: How do you spell your name?
How are you today?

senses.definition: not more than; just

examples.text: It only costs two pounds.

senses.definition: with no others of the same kind

examples.text: She is an only child.

senses.definition: to have an opinion or believe something

examples.text: I think it's going to rain.
I thought you were at school.

senses.usageNote: For a negative idea, English usually says 'I don't think it will rain' rather than 'I think it won't rain'.

senses.definition: to use your mind to consider something

examples.text: Let me think about it.

senses.definition: a period of twelve months

examples.text: My brother is ten years old.

senses.definition: at this time

examples.text: I'm busy now. Call me later.

translations.zh: 我现在很忙，晚点打给我。

senses.definition: to move towards the speaker or to a place

examples.text: Come here, please.

senses.definition: coming before all the others

examples.text: It was my first day at school.

senses.definition: before anything else

examples.text: First, wash your hands.

senses.definition: recently made or bought, or not known before

examples.text: I have a new bike.

senses.definition: to notice things with your eyes

examples.text: I can see the sea from my window.

translations.zh: 从我的窗户可以看到大海。

examples.text: We saw a rainbow yesterday.

senses.usageNote: 'See' means your eyes notice something; 'look at' means you choose to point your eyes at it; 'watch' is for things that move, like TV.

senses.definition: used to compare two things or people

examples.text: My brother is taller than me.

senses.definition: after that; next

examples.text: We had lunch, then we went swimming.

translations.zh: 我们吃了午饭，然后去游泳了。

senses.definition: at that time

examples.text: I was only six then.

senses.definition: in a good or right way

examples.text: She speaks English very well.

senses.usageNote: 'Good' is an adjective and 'well' is an adverb: 'a good singer' but 'she sings well'.

senses.definition: healthy; not ill

examples.text: I don't feel well today.

senses.definition: as well; in addition

examples.text: She plays the piano and also sings.

senses.usageNote: 'Also' usually goes before the main verb or after 'be': 'I also like it', 'He is also tall'.

senses.definition: a period of 24 hours

examples.text: There are seven days in a week.

senses.definition: the time when it is light outside

examples.text: Owls sleep during the day.

senses.definition: nice, pleasant or of a high level

examples.text: This is a good book.
She is good at maths.

senses.usageNote: 'Good' is an adjective; the adverb is 'well'. Say 'She sings well', not 'She sings good'. Use 'good at' for skills.

senses.definition: above something, or from one side to the other

examples.text: The plane flew over our house.

translations.zh: 飞机从我们家上空飞过。

senses.definition: more than

examples.text: There were over a hundred people.

senses.definition: men, women and children; more than one person

examples.text: There were a lot of people at the beach.

senses.usageNote: 'People' is plural: say 'people are', not 'people is'. For one, say 'a person'.

senses.definition: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger

examples.text: The film was very funny.

senses.usageNote: Use 'very much' with verbs, not 'very': 'I like it very much', not 'I very like it'.

senses.definition: the road or direction you take to get somewhere

examples.text: Can you tell me the way to the station?

translations.zh: 你能告诉我去车站的路吗？

senses.definition: how you do something

examples.text: This is the best way to learn words.

translations.zh: 这是学单词的最好方法。

senses.definition: for the reason that

examples.text: I stayed home because it was raining.

senses.usageNote: In writing, avoid starting a sentence with 'Because' unless the main clause follows: 'Because it rained, we stayed in.'

senses.definition: to wish to have or do something

examples.text: I want a glass of water.

senses.usageNote: Say 'want to do': 'I want to go home', not 'I want go home'. 'I'd like' is more polite.

senses.definition: later than something

examples.text: Let's play after lunch.

senses.definition: to let someone have something

examples.text: Give me your hand.
She gave me a book.

senses.definition: to turn your eyes towards something so you can see it

examples.text: Look at this picture.

senses.usageNote: Use 'at' before the thing you see: 'look at the board'. 'See' is what happens without trying; 'watch' is for things that move, like TV.

senses.definition: to seem; to appear

examples.text: You look happy today.

senses.definition: a large number of

examples.text: How many brothers do you have?

senses.usageNote: Use 'many' with plural nouns (many books) and 'much' with uncountable nouns (much water).

senses.definition: used to say what is the right or best thing to do

examples.text: You should drink more water.

senses.usageNote: Don't use 'to' after 'should': 'You should go', not 'You should to go'.

senses.definition: some, used in questions and negative sentences

examples.text: Do you have any brothers?

senses.usageNote: Use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in most questions and negatives: 'I have some', 'I don't have any'.

senses.definition: in, at or to this place

examples.text: Come here, please.
Here is your coffee.

senses.definition: a large amount of

examples.text: How much is this T-shirt?
I don't have much time.

senses.usageNote: 'Much' is common in questions and negatives. In positive sentences, 'a lot of' sounds more natural.

senses.definition: an object, or an idea or event, when you don't need to give its name

examples.text: Put your things in the bag.

senses.definition: to do something with a thing for a purpose

examples.text: Can I use your phone?

translations.zh: 我能用一下你的手机吗？

senses.definition: to do a job, especially to earn money

examples.text: She works at a hospital.

senses.definition: to function correctly

examples.text: The lift isn't working.

senses.definition: to the place where you were before

examples.text: I'll be back in five minutes.

senses.definition: the part of your body from your neck to your bottom, on the other side from your chest

examples.text: My back hurts.

senses.definition: to or in a lower place

examples.text: Please sit down.

senses.definition: the one before now, or at the end

examples.text: I saw him last week.
This is the last train tonight.

senses.usageNote: No 'the' in 'last week', 'last year': say 'I went there last year', not 'the last year'.

senses.definition: measuring a lot from one end to the other, or taking a lot of time

examples.text: It's a long way to the sea.
How long is the film?

senses.definition: an adult male person

examples.text: A man is waiting at the door.

senses.definition: almost all; the biggest number or amount

examples.text: Most children like sweets.

senses.usageNote: Say 'most people', not 'most of people'. Use 'most of' before 'the', 'my' etc.: 'most of my friends'.

senses.definition: to have to have something, or to have to do something

examples.text: I need a new pen.
You need to sleep more.

senses.definition: away from a place or surface; not working or not switched on

examples.text: Please turn off the TV.
Take off your shoes.

senses.definition: having lived or existed for a long time; not new

examples.text: This is a very old town.

translations.zh: 这是一座很古老的小镇。

examples.text: How old are you?

senses.definition: correct or true

examples.text: That's the right answer.

senses.definition: the side of your body that is towards the east when you face north

examples.text: Turn right at the bank.

senses.definition: a thing, when you do not know or say what it is

examples.text: I want to tell you something.

senses.definition: used to make a noun stronger; very

examples.text: It was such a nice day.

senses.usageNote: Use 'such a' before a noun (such a nice day) and 'so' before an adjective alone (so nice).

senses.definition: to give information to someone by speaking

examples.text: Can you tell me the time?

translations.zh: 你能告诉我现在几点吗？

examples.text: She told us a story.

translations.zh: 她给我们讲了一个故事。

senses.usageNote: 'Tell' needs a person after it: 'tell me', 'tell your friend'. Don't say 'tell to me'.

senses.definition: more than is good or needed

examples.text: This coffee is too hot to drink.

senses.usageNote: 'Too' shows a problem: 'too hot to drink'. 'Very' just makes it stronger: 'very hot'.

senses.definition: also

examples.text: I like cats, and my sister does too.

translations.zh: 我喜欢猫，我妹妹也喜欢。

senses.definition: used to ask in or to what place

examples.text: Where do you live?

senses.definition: to see or get something that you were looking for

examples.text: I can't find my keys.
She found a coin on the floor.
examples.cloze: She {{found}} a coin on the floor.

translations.zh: 她在地上发现了一枚硬币。

senses.usageNote: 'Look for' is the action of searching; 'find' is the result. 'I looked for my pen but didn't find it.'

senses.definition: the earth and all the people and places on it

examples.text: I want to travel around the world.

senses.definition: from one side or end of something to the other

examples.text: We walked through the forest.

senses.definition: to say or write a question to someone

examples.text: Can I ask you a question?

senses.usageNote: 'Ask for' means to request something: 'ask for help'. Do not say 'ask to him'; say 'ask him'.

senses.definition: earlier than something

examples.text: Wash your hands before dinner.

senses.definition: to phone someone

examples.text: I'll call you tonight.

senses.definition: to give someone or something a name

examples.text: We called the puppy Max.

translations.zh: 我们给小狗取名叫麦克斯。

senses.definition: very good; excellent

examples.text: We had a great time.

senses.definition: very large or important

examples.text: The Great Wall is very long.

senses.definition: to make it easier for someone to do something

examples.text: Can you help me with my bag?
She helped her brother do his homework.

senses.usageNote: Say 'help someone do' or 'help someone with something', not 'help someone doing'.

senses.definition: the time when a person or animal is alive; the way someone lives

examples.text: She has a busy life.

senses.definition: small in size, or young

examples.text: They live in a little house.

translations.zh: 他们住在一座小房子里。

senses.definition: a small amount of something

examples.text: Add a little salt.

senses.definition: used to say that something is necessary

examples.text: You must wear a seat belt.

senses.usageNote: 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed. 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary.

senses.definition: not at any time; not once

examples.text: I never drink coffee.

senses.usageNote: Don't use 'not' with 'never': 'I never eat meat', not 'I don't never eat meat'.

senses.definition: coming straight after this one

examples.text: See you next week.
The bank is next to the café.

senses.usageNote: No 'the' in 'next week', 'next year' when you mean the one after now.

senses.definition: a particular area, building, town or position

examples.text: This is a nice place for lunch.

translations.zh: 这是个吃午饭的好地方。

senses.definition: continuing until now, or until a particular time

examples.text: Are you still hungry?

senses.definition: to make an effort to do something

examples.text: I tried to call you.

senses.definition: to taste or use something to see if you like it

examples.text: Try this cake. It's delicious!

senses.definition: used to ask for the reason for something

examples.text: Why are you late?

senses.definition: at all times; on every occasion

examples.text: She always drinks tea in the morning.

senses.definition: to have a feeling, like happy, sad, hot or ill

examples.text: I feel tired today.
She felt better after a rest.

translations.zh: 休息之后她感觉好些了。

senses.usageNote: Use an adjective after 'feel': 'I feel good', not 'I feel well good'. Don't say 'I am feeling myself tired'.

senses.definition: one piece or section of something bigger

examples.text: The first part of the film was boring.

translations.zh: 电影的第一部分很无聊。

senses.usageNote: 'Take part in' means to join an activity: 'She took part in the race.'

senses.definition: to move something into a place or position

examples.text: Put your bag on the chair.

senses.definition: a building where people live

examples.text: They bought a house near the river.

translations.zh: 他们在河边买了一栋房子。

senses.usageNote: A 'house' is the building; a 'home' is where you feel you belong.

senses.definition: one more time

examples.text: Please say that again.

senses.definition: one more, or a different one

examples.text: Can I have another biscuit?

translations.zh: 我可以再吃一块饼干吗？

senses.usageNote: 'Another' is followed by a singular noun: 'another book', not 'another books'.

senses.definition: on every side of something, or in a circle

examples.text: We sat around the table.

senses.definition: a little more or less than a number

examples.text: Come at around six o'clock.

senses.definition: better than all the others

examples.text: She is my best friend.

senses.definition: in the space in the middle of two things or people

examples.text: The shop is between the bank and the café.

translations.zh: 商店在银行和咖啡馆之间。

senses.definition: large in size

examples.text: They live in a big house.

translations.zh: 他们住在一栋大房子里。

senses.definition: to become different, or to make something different

examples.text: The town has changed a lot.

senses.definition: the money you get back when you pay more than something costs

examples.text: Here is your change.

senses.definition: a young person who is not yet an adult

examples.text: Every child needs love.

senses.definition: a business that makes or sells things

examples.text: My dad works for a computer company.

translations.zh: 我爸爸在一家电脑公司工作。

senses.definition: not the same

examples.text: My sister and I are very different.

senses.usageNote: In British English say 'different from', e.g. 'This is different from that.'

senses.definition: every one of two or more things, seen one by one

examples.text: Each student has a book.

senses.usageNote: 'Each' is followed by a singular noun and verb: 'Each child has...', not 'Each children have...'.

senses.definition: the last part of something

examples.text: I loved the end of the story.

translations.zh: 我很喜欢这个故事的结尾。

senses.usageNote: 'At the end' means the final point of something; 'in the end' means 'finally, after a long time'.

senses.definition: to finish

examples.text: The party ends at nine.

senses.definition: all the people or things in a group, one by one

examples.text: I brush my teeth every day.

senses.usageNote: 'Every day' (two words) means each day; 'everyday' (one word) is an adjective meaning ordinary.

senses.definition: a number of people or things together

examples.text: Work in groups of four.

senses.definition: the part at the end of your arm with fingers

examples.text: Put up your hand if you know.

senses.definition: a long way above the ground, or bigger than usual

examples.text: That mountain is very high.
Prices are high in this shop.

senses.usageNote: Use 'tall' for people and trees, and 'high' for mountains, walls and prices.

senses.definition: the place where you live

examples.text: I stayed at home all day.

senses.definition: to or at the place where you live

examples.text: What time do you get home?

senses.usageNote: No 'to' before 'home' as an adverb: 'go home', 'come home'.

senses.definition: to have something and not give it away, or to make something stay the same

examples.text: You can keep the book.
She kept the door open.

senses.usageNote: 'Keep doing' means continue: 'Keep walking', not 'Keep to walk'.

senses.definition: to allow someone to do something

examples.text: My mum lets me stay up late on Saturdays.
Let's go to the beach!

senses.usageNote: No 'to' after 'let': 'Let me help', not 'Let me to help'.

senses.definition: to have your home in a place

examples.text: I live in Guangzhou.

senses.usageNote: Use 'in' for towns and countries: 'live in China', not 'live at China'.

senses.definition: 'a lot' or 'lots' means a large number or amount

examples.text: She has a lot of friends.
Thanks a lot!

senses.definition: the word that someone or something is called

examples.text: What's your name?

senses.definition: a word or sign like 1, 2 or 3 that shows how many

examples.text: What's your phone number?

senses.definition: belonging to a particular person

examples.text: I want my own room.
She lives on her own.

senses.usageNote: 'Own' always comes after 'my', 'your' etc.: 'my own bike', not 'an own bike'.

senses.definition: to do things for fun, or to take part in a game or sport

examples.text: The kids are playing football outside.

senses.usageNote: Use 'play' with ball games (play tennis) and 'play the' with music (play the guitar). Use 'go' with -ing sports: go swimming.

senses.definition: a story that actors perform in a theatre

examples.text: We saw a funny play last night.

translations.zh: 我们昨晚看了一部有趣的话剧。

senses.definition: to show where something is with your finger

examples.text: She pointed at the map.

senses.definition: a mark you get in a game or test

examples.text: Our team won by two points.

senses.definition: very, or very much

examples.text: I really like your new haircut.

translations.zh: 我真的很喜欢你的新发型。

senses.definition: used to show you are surprised

examples.text: 'I've got a pet snake.' 'Really?'

senses.definition: exactly like another, or not a different one

examples.text: We go to the same school.

translations.zh: 我们在同一所学校上学。

senses.usageNote: Always use 'the' before 'same', and 'as' after it: 'the same as yours'.

senses.definition: to let someone see something

examples.text: Show me your new phone!

senses.definition: a programme on TV or a performance in a theatre

examples.text: We watched a cooking show.

translations.zh: 我们看了一个烹饪节目。

senses.definition: not large in size or amount

examples.text: They live in a small flat.

translations.zh: 他们住在一套小公寓里。

senses.definition: below something, or covered by it

examples.text: The cat is under the bed.

senses.definition: less than a number or age

examples.text: Children under five get in free.

translations.zh: 五岁以下儿童免费入场。

senses.definition: during the time that something else is happening

examples.text: I listen to music while I cook.

senses.definition: a period of time

examples.text: Can you wait a while?

senses.definition: an adult female person

examples.text: A woman asked me the way to the bank.

translations.zh: 一位女士向我问去银行的路。

senses.usageNote: The plural 'women' is said /ˈwɪmɪn/.

senses.definition: a single unit of language that has a meaning

examples.text: What does this word mean?

senses.definition: used to agree, say something is true, or accept something

examples.text: 'Are you ready?' 'Yes, I am.'

translations.zh: “你准备好了吗？”“是的，准备好了。”

senses.usageNote: To agree with a negative question, English uses 'no': 'You're not hungry?' 'No, I'm not.' Chinese often says 对 here.

senses.definition: coins and notes used to buy things

examples.text: I don't have enough money for the ticket.

senses.usageNote: Uncountable. Say 'a lot of money' or 'much money', never 'many moneys'.

senses.definition: an area of land with its own government

examples.text: She has lived in four countries.

senses.definition: land outside towns and cities

examples.text: We spent the weekend in the country.

translations.zh: 我们在乡下度过了周末。

senses.definition: any thing at all

examples.text: I didn't buy anything.

senses.definition: to or at a distance from a place or person

examples.text: The school is two kilometres away.

senses.definition: to start to be something

examples.text: She wants to become a vet.

senses.definition: more good than something else

examples.text: This pen is better than that one.

senses.definition: less ill than before

examples.text: I feel much better today.

senses.definition: the two people or things together

examples.text: Both my parents are teachers.

senses.usageNote: 'Both' is for two only. For three or more, use 'all'.

senses.definition: a small number of people or things

examples.text: I stayed there for a few days.
Very few people came.

senses.usageNote: 'A few' means some (positive). 'Few' alone means not many (negative). Use it with plural nouns; for uncountable nouns use 'a little'.

senses.definition: an activity or sport that you play for fun, with rules

examples.text: Let's play a game.
Did you watch the game last night?

senses.definition: the top part of your body, where your eyes and brain are

examples.text: He hit his head on the door.

senses.definition: to have something in your hand or arms

examples.text: Hold my hand when we cross.
He held the baby carefully.

senses.definition: big in size or amount

examples.text: I'd like a large coffee, please.

senses.usageNote: 'Large' is a false friend for some learners: it means big, not wide.

senses.definition: to have a meaning; to say something in other words

examples.text: What does this word mean?

senses.usageNote: Ask 'What does it mean?', not 'What is it mean?'.

senses.definition: unkind to other people

examples.text: Don't be mean to your sister.

senses.definition: to go to a different place or position, or to put something in a different place

examples.text: Can you move your chair?

senses.definition: to go to live in a new home

examples.text: We moved to a new flat.

translations.zh: 我们搬进了一套新公寓。

senses.definition: to move something so that it is no longer closed

examples.text: Open your books at page ten.

senses.definition: not closed, so people can go in or use it

examples.text: Is the shop open on Sunday?

senses.definition: to ask for food, drinks or goods that you want to buy

examples.text: Are you ready to order?

senses.definition: the way things are arranged, one after another

examples.text: Put the words in the right order.

translations.zh: 把这些词按正确顺序排列。

senses.definition: to move very fast on your legs

examples.text: The dog is running in the garden.
I ran to catch the bus.

senses.definition: a place where children go to learn

examples.text: I walk to school every day.

senses.usageNote: Say 'go to school' and 'at school' with no 'the' when you mean studying there.

senses.definition: the left or right part of something, or one of its surfaces

examples.text: Write on both sides of the paper.

senses.definition: from a time in the past until now

examples.text: I've lived here since 2020.

translations.zh: 我从2020年起就住在这里了。

senses.usageNote: Use 'since' with a starting point (since Monday) and 'for' with a length of time (for three days).

senses.definition: to begin doing something, or to begin to happen

examples.text: The film starts at seven.

senses.definition: a period of seven days

examples.text: I play football twice a week.

senses.definition: not having or not using something

examples.text: I can't see without my glasses.

senses.definition: to make letters or words on paper or a screen

examples.text: Write your name at the top.
She wrote a letter to her grandma.
examples.cloze: She {{wrote}} a letter to her grandma.

senses.definition: a group of people who are related to each other

examples.text: My whole family came to the wedding.

translations.zh: 我全家都来参加婚礼了。

senses.definition: a large town

examples.text: Bangkok is a huge city.

translations.zh: 曼谷是一座巨大的城市。

senses.definition: something that is difficult and needs to be dealt with

examples.text: There's a problem with my computer.

senses.usageNote: A 'problem' is a difficulty; a 'question' is something you ask. Don't say 'I have a question with my phone' when it is broken.

senses.definition: to go away from a place or person

examples.text: The train leaves at six.

senses.definition: to let something stay where it is, often by mistake

examples.text: I left my keys at the office.

translations.zh: 我把钥匙忘在办公室了。

senses.definition: one of the separate parts inside a building, with walls and a door

examples.text: My room is next to the bathroom.

senses.definition: enough space for something

examples.text: Is there room for one more person?

senses.usageNote: In this meaning 'room' is uncountable: 'no room', not 'no rooms'.

senses.definition: the dark part of the day, when most people sleep

examples.text: It rained all night.

senses.definition: the clear liquid that falls as rain and that people drink

examples.text: Could I have a glass of water?

senses.definition: to pour water on plants

examples.text: Remember to water the plants.

senses.definition: having a big effect, or mattering a lot

examples.text: It's important to review every day.

senses.definition: playing on the other side in a game or sport

examples.text: We played against a very good team.

translations.zh: 我们和一支很强的队比赛。

senses.definition: touching something and leaning on it

examples.text: The bike is against the wall.

senses.definition: a part of a place, town or country

examples.text: There are many parks in this area.

senses.definition: a set of printed pages fixed together inside a cover

examples.text: I'm reading a good book.

senses.definition: to arrange to have a seat, room or ticket at a later time

examples.text: We booked a table for four.

senses.definition: to take someone or something with you to a place

examples.text: Please bring your lunch tomorrow.

senses.usageNote: 'Bring' means towards the speaker's place; 'take' means away from it: 'Bring it here', 'Take it to school'.

senses.definition: the work of buying and selling things to make money

examples.text: My mum runs a small business.

translations.zh: 我妈妈经营一家小公司。

senses.definition: a set of lessons about one subject

examples.text: She's doing an English course.

senses.usageNote: 'Of course' means 'yes, certainly': 'Can I sit here?' 'Of course!'

senses.definition: all through a period of time, or at some point in it

examples.text: Please don't talk during the film.

senses.usageNote: 'During' answers 'when?' and 'for' answers 'how long?': 'during the summer', 'for two weeks'.

senses.definition: at any time

examples.text: Have you ever seen snow?

senses.definition: something that shows what other things of the same kind are like

examples.text: Can you give me an example?

senses.definition: a long way from here or from another place

examples.text: Is the station far from here?
We didn't walk very far.

senses.usageNote: In positive sentences, 'a long way' sounds more natural: 'It's a long way', not 'It's far' alone.

senses.definition: to take place, often without being planned

examples.text: What happened to your arm?

senses.usageNote: 'Happen' has no passive form. Say 'An accident happened', not 'An accident was happened'.

senses.definition: to notice sounds with your ears

examples.text: Can you hear me?
I heard a noise outside.

senses.usageNote: 'Hear' is about sound reaching you; 'listen to' means you try to hear. 'I listened but didn't hear anything.'

senses.definition: a plan or thought that comes into your mind

examples.text: That's a good idea!
I have no idea where he is.

senses.definition: to have something as one of the parts

examples.text: Does the price include breakfast?

senses.definition: facts or details about something

examples.text: I need some information about trains.

translations.zh: 我需要一些火车的信息。

senses.usageNote: 'Information' is uncountable: 'some information' or 'a piece of information', not 'an information' or 'informations'.

senses.definition: the work you do regularly to get money

examples.text: My sister has a new job.

translations.zh: 我姐姐找到了一份新工作。

senses.usageNote: 'Job' is countable (a job); 'work' is usually uncountable. Say 'I'm looking for a job' or 'I'm looking for work'.

senses.definition: friendly and caring towards other people

examples.text: It's very kind of you to help.

senses.definition: a type or sort

examples.text: What kind of music do you like?

senses.definition: a long thin mark, or a row of people or things

examples.text: Draw a line under the title.

senses.definition: to like something very much, or to care a lot about someone

examples.text: I love my grandparents.
We love swimming.

senses.definition: a place where people buy and sell food and other things, often outside

examples.text: We buy vegetables at the market.

senses.definition: to come together with someone, or to see someone for the first time

examples.text: Nice to meet you.
We met at the station.

senses.usageNote: No 'with' is needed: 'I'll meet you at six', not 'I'll meet with you at six'.

senses.definition: a person who belongs to a group, club or team

examples.text: She is a member of the chess club.

translations.zh: 她是国际象棋俱乐部的成员。

senses.definition: one of the twelve parts of a year, like January or May

examples.text: I'm going to Beijing next month.

senses.definition: not anything

examples.text: There's nothing in the box.

senses.definition: many times

examples.text: I often walk to school.
How often do you play tennis?

senses.usageNote: 'Often' usually goes before the main verb but after 'be': 'I often read', 'She is often late'.

senses.definition: one time

examples.text: I go swimming once a week.
Once upon a time, there was a little bear.

senses.definition: something you ask to get an answer

examples.text: Can I ask you a question?

translations.zh: 我可以问你一个问题吗？

senses.usageNote: Say 'ask a question', not 'ask a problem'.

senses.definition: to look at words and understand them

examples.text: I read a story to my little brother.

translations.zh: 我给弟弟读了一个故事。

senses.definition: coming after the first one

examples.text: This is my second visit to London.

senses.definition: a very short unit of time; there are 60 in a minute

examples.text: Wait a second, please.

senses.definition: certain; having no doubt

examples.text: Are you sure the shop is open?

senses.definition: yes; of course

examples.text: 'Can you help me?' 'Sure!'

senses.definition: to change direction, or to move round

examples.text: Turn left at the end of the road.

senses.definition: the time when a person can or must do something

examples.text: It's your turn to choose a game.

senses.definition: having the colour of snow or milk

examples.text: I have a white cat.

senses.definition: a paper or web page with spaces where you write information

examples.text: Write your name on the form.

translations.zh: 在表格上写上你的名字。

senses.definition: a type or kind of something

examples.text: Walking is a good form of exercise.

translations.zh: 散步是一种很好的运动方式。

senses.definition: a period of sixty minutes

examples.text: The trip takes two hours.
I waited for an hour.

senses.usageNote: The 'h' is silent, so we say 'an hour', not 'a hour'.

senses.definition: a smaller amount of something

examples.text: You should eat less sugar.

senses.usageNote: Use 'less' with uncountable nouns (less water) and 'fewer' with plural nouns (fewer people).

senses.definition: the brightness from the sun or a lamp that lets you see

examples.text: Please turn on the light.

senses.definition: not heavy

examples.text: This bag is very light.

senses.definition: a period of sixty seconds

examples.text: Wait a minute, please.
The bus comes in five minutes.

senses.definition: a man, woman or child

examples.text: She is a very kind person.

translations.zh: 她是一个非常善良的人。

senses.definition: to appear to be something

examples.text: You seem tired today.

senses.definition: to spend time learning about a subject

examples.text: She studies English every evening.

senses.usageNote: 'Study' is about the effort; 'learn' is about getting the knowledge. You study for a test to learn the words.

senses.definition: to speak to someone and share ideas or news

examples.text: We talked for hours.

senses.usageNote: Say 'talk to someone' or 'talk about something'.

senses.definition: on this day

examples.text: It's very hot today.

senses.definition: up to a particular time, and then stopping

examples.text: The shop is open until nine.

senses.usageNote: Use 'until' for time, not place: 'I walked to the park', not 'I walked until the park'.

senses.definition: someone you know well and like, who is not family

examples.text: He is my oldest friend.

senses.definition: having the skill or chance to do something

examples.text: She was able to finish the race.

senses.usageNote: Say 'be able to do something', with 'to'. It is often used where 'can' has no form, e.g. 'I will be able to come.'

senses.definition: the front part of your head, where your eyes, nose and mouth are

examples.text: Wash your face before breakfast.
She had a big smile on her face.

translations.zh: 她脸上挂着大大的笑容。

senses.definition: to look towards something or be turned towards it

examples.text: Our room faces the sea.

senses.definition: as much or as many as needed

examples.text: There isn't enough time.
The water is warm enough to swim in.

senses.usageNote: Before a noun: 'enough time'. After an adjective: 'warm enough'. The order is not optional.

senses.definition: to start doing something

examples.text: The lesson begins at nine.

senses.definition: having the darkest colour, like the sky at night

examples.text: She has a black cat.

senses.definition: all the physical parts of a person or animal

examples.text: Exercise is good for your body.

senses.definition: to shut something

examples.text: Please close the window.

senses.definition: near

examples.text: The shop is close to my house.

senses.usageNote: When it means 'near', 'close' is said /kləʊs/, with an 's' sound.

senses.definition: to make something into pieces with a knife or scissors

examples.text: Cut the apple in half.

senses.definition: before the usual or expected time

examples.text: I got up early this morning.

senses.definition: all things

examples.text: Thanks for everything!

senses.definition: something that happens to you

examples.text: The trip was a great experience.

translations.zh: 这次旅行是一次很棒的经历。

senses.definition: knowledge or skill you get from doing something

examples.text: She has a lot of experience with children.

translations.zh: 她在照顾孩子方面很有经验。

senses.usageNote: In the meaning 'skill from doing', 'experience' is uncountable: 'a lot of experience', not 'many experiences'.

senses.definition: one of the two parts of your face that you see with

examples.text: Close your eyes and make a wish.

senses.definition: to go behind someone or something

examples.text: Follow me, please.
Follow the signs to the station.

senses.definition: costing no money

examples.text: The museum is free on Sundays.

senses.definition: not busy; with nothing to do

examples.text: Are you free this afternoon?

senses.usageNote: 'Free time' means time when you are not working or studying.

senses.definition: a female child or young woman

examples.text: There are ten girls in my class.

senses.definition: how well your body and mind are

examples.text: Sleep is good for your health.

senses.definition: things that happened in the past, or the study of them

examples.text: History is my favourite subject.

translations.zh: 历史是我最喜欢的科目。

senses.definition: at a time after now or after that time

examples.text: See you later!

senses.definition: the part of you that thinks and feels

examples.text: I changed my mind.

senses.definition: to be unhappy or worried about something

examples.text: Do you mind if I open the window?

senses.usageNote: To say yes to 'Do you mind...?', answer 'No, not at all', because it means 'I don't mind'.

senses.definition: a woman who is someone's parent

examples.text: My mother is a nurse.

senses.definition: sounds arranged in a pleasant way by singing or playing instruments

examples.text: What music do you like?

senses.definition: not far away from

examples.text: Is there a bank near here?

senses.usageNote: No 'to' after 'near': 'near the school', not 'near to the school' in most cases.

senses.definition: new information about something that has just happened

examples.text: I have some good news!

senses.usageNote: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'The news is good', not 'a news' or 'the news are'.

senses.definition: a room or building where people work at desks

examples.text: My mum works in an office.

senses.definition: an idea about what you are going to do

examples.text: Do you have any plans for the weekend?

senses.definition: to decide what you are going to do and how

examples.text: We planned our trip together.

translations.zh: 我们一起计划了这次旅行。

senses.definition: true and existing, not imagined or false

examples.text: Is that a real diamond?

senses.definition: to say words; to be able to use a language

examples.text: Do you speak Chinese?
I spoke to her yesterday.

senses.usageNote: Use 'speak' with languages: 'speak English', not 'say English' or 'talk English'.

senses.definition: to be on your feet with your body straight up

examples.text: Please stand in a line.
We stood at the bus stop.

senses.definition: to not move or not do something any more

examples.text: The bus stopped outside the school.

senses.usageNote: 'Stop doing' means you don't do it any more; 'stop to do' means you stop so that you can do something else.

senses.definition: a place where a bus or train stops for people

examples.text: Get off at the next stop.

senses.definition: a description of events, true or imagined, told to entertain people

examples.text: Grandma told us a funny story.

translations.zh: 奶奶给我们讲了一个有趣的故事。

senses.definition: with each other; in one group

examples.text: Let's do our homework together.

senses.definition: what you can see from a place, especially beautiful countryside

examples.text: The view from the top of the hill is amazing.

translations.zh: 从山顶看到的景色美极了。

senses.definition: until now; used in questions and negative sentences

examples.text: Have you finished your homework yet?
The bus hasn't come yet.

senses.usageNote: 'Yet' usually goes at the end of the sentence.

senses.definition: not old; having lived for only a short time

examples.text: My mum is younger than my dad.

senses.definition: a person who is studying at a school or university

examples.text: She was my best student that year.

translations.zh: 那年她是我最好的学生。

senses.definition: to gain knowledge or a skill by studying or practising

examples.text: She is learning Thai.
I learned to swim when I was six.

senses.usageNote: 'Learn' is what the student does; 'teach' is what the teacher does. They are not interchangeable.

senses.definition: something that is true and can be shown to be true

examples.text: Here is a fun fact about bees.

translations.zh: 这里有一个关于蜜蜂的有趣事实。

examples.text: In fact, I have never been to London.

translations.zh: 事实上，我从没去过伦敦。

senses.usageNote: 'In fact' is used to add something true or surprising. Do not say 'in the fact'.

senses.definition: a time when people meet to eat, talk and have fun together

examples.text: We're having a party for Tom's birthday.

translations.zh: 我们要为汤姆的生日开个派对。

senses.usageNote: Say 'have a party' or 'go to a party', and 'at a party' for where you are.

senses.definition: to know what something means or why it happens

examples.text: I don't understand this question.

senses.definition: moving on or beside a road, river or line

examples.text: We walked along the river.

senses.definition: not good or not pleasant

examples.text: I had a bad day at school.

translations.zh: 我今天在学校过得很糟糕。

senses.definition: to feel sure that something is true

examples.text: I don't believe his story.

senses.definition: to make something by putting parts together

examples.text: Let's build a sandcastle.

senses.definition: a road vehicle with four wheels and an engine, for a few people

examples.text: We went to the park by car.

senses.definition: a man who is someone's parent

examples.text: My father is a bus driver.

senses.definition: to get bigger or taller over time

examples.text: Plants need sun to grow.

translations.zh: 植物需要阳光才能生长。

examples.text: You have grown so tall!

senses.definition: to plant something and look after it

examples.text: We grow tomatoes in the garden.

translations.zh: 我们在花园里种西红柿。

senses.definition: not easy to do or understand

examples.text: This question is too hard.

senses.definition: firm and not soft

examples.text: The bed is very hard.

senses.definition: with a lot of effort

examples.text: She works hard every day.

senses.definition: to be important

examples.text: It doesn't matter if you are late.
What's the matter?

senses.definition: a very short time; a particular point in time

examples.text: Just a moment, please.
She's busy at the moment.

senses.definition: to give money for something you buy or for work someone does

examples.text: Can I pay by card?
She paid for our lunch.

senses.usageNote: You 'pay for' the thing you buy: 'I paid for the book', not 'I paid the book'.

senses.definition: why something happens or why someone does something

examples.text: What's the reason for the delay?

senses.usageNote: Say 'the reason for something' or 'the reason why', not 'the reason of'.

senses.definition: a person, when you do not know or say who

examples.text: Someone is knocking at the door.

senses.usageNote: Use 'someone' in positive sentences and 'anyone' in most questions and negatives: 'Is anyone there?'

senses.definition: to not leave a place; to remain

examples.text: I stayed at home all day.

senses.definition: to live somewhere for a short time as a visitor

examples.text: We stayed in a hotel near the sea.

translations.zh: 我们住在海边的一家酒店。

senses.definition: a group of people who play a sport or work together

examples.text: Our team won the game.

senses.definition: to stay somewhere until someone comes or something happens

examples.text: Please wait here for a moment.

senses.usageNote: Say 'wait for someone': 'I'm waiting for the bus', not 'waiting the bus'.

senses.definition: the things that people and animals eat

examples.text: The food at that restaurant is excellent.

senses.definition: to keep something in your mind, or to bring it back into your mind

examples.text: I can't remember her name.

senses.usageNote: 'Remember to do' is about a future task; 'remember doing' is about a past event.

senses.definition: to put something together with something else

examples.text: Add some sugar to the milk.

senses.definition: what we breathe; the space around us

examples.text: The air is fresh in the mountains.

senses.definition: nearly, but not completely

examples.text: It's almost time for lunch.

senses.usageNote: Say 'almost all the students', not 'almost students'.

senses.definition: before now, or sooner than expected

examples.text: I have already eaten.

senses.definition: in the middle of a group of people or things

examples.text: The house is among the trees.

senses.usageNote: Use 'between' for two things and 'among' for three or more.

senses.definition: a male child

examples.text: There are ten boys in my class.

senses.definition: to make something go into pieces or stop working

examples.text: Be careful, don't break the glass.

translations.zh: 小心，别把玻璃杯打碎了。

senses.definition: a short time when you stop working or studying to rest

examples.text: Let's take a ten-minute break.

senses.definition: to think that something is important

examples.text: She really cares about animals.

senses.definition: the act of looking after someone or something

examples.text: Take care of your little sister.

senses.definition: a group of students who learn together

examples.text: There are thirty students in my class.

senses.definition: a time when students are taught something

examples.text: I have a maths class at ten.

senses.definition: easy to see, hear or understand

examples.text: Her voice is loud and clear.

senses.definition: with no clouds, or easy to see through

examples.text: The water in the lake is very clear.

senses.definition: to stop living

examples.text: The flowers died because it was too hot.

translations.zh: 因为天太热，花都枯死了。

senses.definition: something important or special that happens

examples.text: The school sports day is a big event.

translations.zh: 学校运动会是一项重大活动。

senses.definition: every person

examples.text: Good morning, everyone!

senses.usageNote: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb: 'Everyone is here', not 'Everyone are here'.

senses.definition: to think that something will happen

examples.text: I expect it will rain later.

senses.definition: holding as much as possible; with no space left

examples.text: The bus was full.
No more cake, thanks. I'm full.

translations.zh: 不要蛋糕了，谢谢。我吃饱了。

senses.usageNote: 'I'm full' means you have eaten enough.

senses.definition: the time that will come after now

examples.text: What do you want to do in the future?

senses.definition: one of two equal parts of something

examples.text: I ate half of the cake.
It's half past three.

senses.definition: to want something to happen and think that it might

examples.text: I hope you feel better soon.

senses.usageNote: Use 'hope' for things that may happen and 'wish' for things that are not true now: 'I wish I could fly'.

senses.definition: the part of the earth that is not sea

examples.text: Frogs live on land and in water.

translations.zh: 青蛙生活在陆地上和水里。

senses.definition: to come down to the ground after flying

examples.text: The plane landed on time.

senses.definition: the words people in a country use to speak and write

examples.text: How many languages can you speak?

senses.definition: after the usual or planned time

examples.text: Sorry I'm late.
Don't be late for school.

senses.usageNote: Say 'late for school', not 'late to school'. 'Lately' means recently, not 'in a late way'.

senses.definition: to not be able to find something

examples.text: Try not to lose your ticket.
I lost my phone yesterday.

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'lose' /luːz/ (verb) with 'loose' /luːs/ (not tight).

senses.definition: to not win a game

examples.text: Our team lost the match.

senses.definition: not high; close to the ground or small in amount

examples.text: The wall is very low.
Prices are low in the market.

senses.definition: most important or biggest

examples.text: The main street is very busy.

senses.definition: a time when people come together to talk about something

examples.text: Dad has a meeting at ten.

senses.definition: to ask if someone would like something, or say you will do something

examples.text: She offered me a cup of tea.
He offered to carry my bag.

senses.definition: the people whose job is to keep people safe and make sure they obey the law

examples.text: The police helped the lost boy.

translations.zh: 警察帮助了那个走失的男孩。

senses.usageNote: 'The police' is plural: 'The police are coming.' For one person, say 'a police officer'.

senses.definition: able to happen or be done

examples.text: Is it possible to walk there?

senses.usageNote: Say 'It is possible for me to come', not 'I am possible to come'.

senses.definition: fairly or rather, but not very

examples.text: The film was quite good.

senses.definition: to come or go back to a place

examples.text: She returned home at six.

senses.usageNote: 'Return' already means 'go back', so don't say 'return back'.

senses.definition: to give or send something back

examples.text: Please return the book next week.

senses.definition: a hard surface that cars and buses drive on

examples.text: Be careful when you cross the road.

senses.definition: more than two, but not very many

examples.text: I've read the book several times.

senses.definition: in a short time from now

examples.text: Dinner will be ready soon.

senses.definition: to use money to buy things

examples.text: I don't spend much money on clothes.

senses.usageNote: Say 'spend money on something' and 'spend time doing something': 'I spent an hour reading.'

senses.definition: to use time doing something or being somewhere

examples.text: We spent the summer at the beach.

translations.zh: 我们在海滩度过了夏天。

senses.definition: to move along by putting one foot in front of the other

examples.text: We walked to the park.

senses.definition: a journey on foot, often for fun

examples.text: Let's go for a walk.

senses.definition: to be the best or first in a game, race or competition

examples.text: I hope our team wins today.

translations.zh: 我希望我们队今天能赢。

examples.text: She won the race.

senses.usageNote: You 'win' a game or prize, but you 'beat' a person or team: 'We beat them 2–0.'

senses.definition: to get something by paying money for it

examples.text: I bought this jacket yesterday.

translations.zh: 这件夹克是我昨天买的。

senses.definition: thin material for writing, drawing or wrapping things

examples.text: Can I have a piece of paper?

senses.usageNote: 'Paper' (the material) is uncountable: say 'a piece of paper' or 'a sheet of paper', not 'a paper'.

senses.definition: a newspaper

examples.text: My dad reads the paper every morning.

translations.zh: 我爸爸每天早上看报纸。

senses.definition: the early part of the day, from when the sun rises until noon

examples.text: I run every morning before work.

senses.definition: from one side of something to the other

examples.text: We walked across the bridge.

senses.definition: the middle of something

examples.text: We live near the city centre.

senses.usageNote: British spelling is 'centre'; American spelling is 'center'.

senses.definition: to choose what you are going to do after thinking

examples.text: We decided to stay at home.

senses.usageNote: Say 'decide to do something', not 'decide doing something'.

senses.definition: after a time; used when you say what time it is

examples.text: It's ten past three.

senses.definition: the time before now

examples.text: In the past, people wrote letters.

senses.definition: to stop doing things and relax or sleep

examples.text: Let's rest for ten minutes.

senses.definition: the part that is left; the others

examples.text: I'll eat the rest of the pizza later.

translations.zh: 剩下的披萨我待会儿吃。

senses.definition: to rest your body on a chair or on the ground

examples.text: Please sit next to me.
We sat on the grass.

senses.definition: different from usual and often better or more important

examples.text: Today is a special day for our family.

translations.zh: 今天对我们家来说是个特别的日子。

senses.definition: a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs

examples.text: The keys are on the table.

senses.definition: a set of questions to find out what someone knows

examples.text: We have a spelling test tomorrow.

senses.usageNote: Say 'take a test' or 'do a test', and 'pass' or 'fail' it.

senses.definition: the highest part of something

examples.text: We climbed to the top of the hill.

senses.definition: a place with houses and shops, bigger than a village but smaller than a city

examples.text: I live in a small town by the sea.

translations.zh: 我住在海边的一个小镇上。

senses.definition: one side of a sheet of paper in a book, magazine or notebook

examples.text: Please open your books at page ten.

senses.usageNote: Say 'on page 5' for where something is, and 'turn to page 5' or 'open at page 5' for finding it.

senses.definition: used to say what is really true, often when it is a surprise

examples.text: Actually, I don't like tea.

senses.usageNote: 'Actually' does not mean 'now' or 'at present'. Use 'currently' for that.

senses.definition: how old someone or something is

examples.text: We are the same age.

senses.definition: any person at all

examples.text: Is anyone at home?

senses.definition: paintings, drawings and other beautiful things that people make

examples.text: Art is my favourite subject.

translations.zh: 美术是我最喜欢的科目。

senses.definition: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or school

examples.text: That is the tallest building in the city.

senses.definition: to hold something and take it with you

examples.text: Can you carry this bag for me?

senses.definition: a time when you are able to do something

examples.text: I didn't get a chance to say goodbye.

senses.definition: to have a price of

examples.text: How much does this cost?

senses.definition: the amount of money you need to pay for something

examples.text: The cost of the trip is fifty pounds.

translations.zh: 这次旅行的费用是五十英镑。

senses.definition: the way in which two things are not the same

examples.text: What's the difference between these two words?

senses.definition: the thing you open and close to go into a room or building

examples.text: Someone is at the door.

senses.definition: to control a car, bus or lorry and make it move

examples.text: My mum drives me to school.

senses.definition: to put food in your mouth and swallow it

examples.text: We eat rice every day.

senses.definition: used after a negative to mean 'also'

examples.text: I don't like it either.

senses.usageNote: Use 'too' in positive sentences and 'either' in negative ones: 'I like it too', 'I don't like it either'.

senses.definition: one or the other of two

examples.text: You can sit on either side.

senses.definition: other, or more

examples.text: Do you want anything else?

senses.usageNote: 'Else' comes after words like 'something', 'anyone', 'what' and 'where': 'someone else', 'what else'.

senses.definition: to go down to the ground suddenly, without wanting to

examples.text: Be careful or you will fall.

translations.zh: 小心点，不然你会摔倒的。

examples.text: The leaves fell from the trees.

senses.usageNote: 'Fall' does not take an object. Say 'I dropped my phone', not 'I fell my phone'.

senses.definition: the surface of the earth that you stand on outside

examples.text: The ball fell to the ground.

senses.definition: a set of words or names written one below another

examples.text: I made a shopping list.

senses.definition: perhaps; possibly

examples.text: Maybe it will snow tomorrow.

senses.definition: a short piece of writing to help you remember something, or a short letter

examples.text: I left a note on the table.
Take notes in class.

senses.definition: not in a building; in the open air

examples.text: The children are playing outside.

senses.definition: a drawing, painting or photo

examples.text: Look at the picture on page six.

senses.definition: a person who plays a game or sport

examples.text: He is the best player in our team.

translations.zh: 他是我们队里最好的球员。

senses.definition: a show on television or radio

examples.text: My favourite TV programme starts at eight.

translations.zh: 我最喜欢的电视节目八点开始。

senses.definition: having the colour of blood or a ripe tomato

examples.text: She has a red coat.

senses.definition: to make a letter, message or parcel go to someone

examples.text: I'll send you a message later.
She sent me a birthday card.

senses.definition: small in length, height or time

examples.text: She has short hair.
My brother is short, but I'm tall.

translations.zh: 我哥哥个子矮，但我个子高。

senses.definition: on some occasions, but not always

examples.text: I sometimes walk to work.

senses.definition: something that you hear

examples.text: I heard a strange sound outside.

translations.zh: 我听到外面有奇怪的声音。

senses.definition: to seem, from what you hear or read

examples.text: That sounds like a great idea!

senses.definition: an empty area that you can use

examples.text: There isn't enough space in my bag.

translations.zh: 我包里没有足够的空间。

senses.definition: the area outside the earth where the stars and planets are

examples.text: She wants to travel into space.

senses.definition: right or correct; not false

examples.text: Is it true that you can speak French?

senses.definition: in most cases; most of the time

examples.text: I usually get up at seven.

senses.definition: to go to see a person or a place

examples.text: We visited our aunt at the weekend.

translations.zh: 我们周末去看望了姑姑。

senses.usageNote: 'Visit' needs no preposition: 'visit Paris', not 'visit to Paris'. The noun uses 'to': 'a visit to Paris'.

senses.definition: to look at something for some time, especially something that moves

examples.text: We watched a film last night.

translations.zh: 我们昨晚看了一部电影。

senses.definition: a small clock that you wear on your wrist

examples.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

senses.definition: the woman a man is married to

examples.text: This is my wife, Sarah.

senses.definition: not correct

examples.text: Sorry, I think you have the wrong number.

translations.zh: 对不起，我想你打错电话了。

senses.definition: causing a problem

examples.text: What's wrong with your leg?

senses.definition: feeling pleased and satisfied

examples.text: I'm happy you could come.

senses.definition: something that you do

examples.text: I like action films.

senses.definition: a place where people keep their money safe

examples.text: Dad went to the bank this morning.

translations.zh: 爸爸今天早上去了银行。

senses.definition: the ground at the side of a river

examples.text: We had a picnic on the river bank.

senses.definition: at the back of something

examples.text: The cat is hiding behind the sofa.

senses.definition: a flat surface on a wall that a teacher writes on

examples.text: Look at the words on the board.

senses.definition: a flat piece of wood or card used for games

examples.text: Let's play a board game.

senses.definition: to look at something to make sure it is correct or safe

examples.text: Check your answers before you finish.

translations.zh: 做完之前检查一下你的答案。

senses.definition: an area of open land, often with grass or crops

examples.text: The horses are in the field.
We played football on the field.

senses.definition: the heat, light and flames made when something burns

examples.text: We sat around the fire and sang.

translations.zh: 我们围坐在火堆旁唱歌。

senses.definition: the part inside your chest that pushes blood around your body

examples.text: Exercise makes your heart strong.
I learnt the poem by heart.

senses.definition: a small piece of metal used to open or lock a door

examples.text: I lost my house key.

senses.definition: one of the buttons on a keyboard or piano

examples.text: Press any key to start.

senses.definition: on the side of your body where your heart is

examples.text: I write with my left hand.
Turn left at the bank.

senses.definition: a written message that you send by post

examples.text: I wrote a letter to my pen friend.

senses.definition: a sign that stands for a sound, like A, B or C

examples.text: There are 26 letters in the English alphabet.

senses.definition: to succeed in a test or exam

examples.text: I hope I pass my English test.

translations.zh: 我希望能通过英语考试。

senses.usageNote: Chinese speakers sometimes say 'pass the exam' when they mean 'take the exam'. 'Take' means you do it; 'pass' means you do it successfully.

senses.definition: to give something to someone with your hand

examples.text: Could you pass me the salt, please?

senses.definition: a polite word you use when you ask for something

examples.text: Can I have some water, please?

senses.usageNote: In English, 'please' makes requests polite. Leaving it out can sound rude, even when Chinese would not need '请'.

senses.definition: the amount of money you must pay to buy something

examples.text: The price of this bag is too high.

senses.usageNote: Prices are 'high' or 'low', not 'expensive' or 'cheap'. Things are expensive or cheap.

senses.definition: almost certainly; very likely

examples.text: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

senses.definition: shaped like a circle or a ball

examples.text: We have a round table in the kitchen.

translations.zh: 我们厨房里有一张圆桌。

senses.definition: on every side of something; in a circle

examples.text: We sat round the fire.

senses.definition: something that tells you what you must or must not do

examples.text: You must follow the school rules.

senses.definition: a road in a town with buildings on one or both sides

examples.text: There's a café on our street.

translations.zh: 我们街上有一家咖啡馆。

senses.usageNote: British English says 'in the street' or 'on the street' for where something happens.

senses.definition: the sound you make when you speak or sing

examples.text: She has a beautiful voice.

senses.usageNote: 'Voice' is for people; for other things use 'sound' or 'noise'.

senses.definition: to have clothes, shoes or glasses on your body

examples.text: She wears glasses.
He wore a red jacket.

senses.usageNote: 'Wear' is the state (穿着); 'put on' is the action (穿上): 'Put on your coat.'

senses.definition: not difficult; needing little effort

examples.text: The test was easier than I expected.

senses.definition: not easy; needing effort or skill

examples.text: Thai tones are difficult for beginners.

translations.zh: 泰语声调对初学者来说很难。

senses.definition: what you say or write back to a question

examples.text: I know the answer!

senses.definition: to say or write something back to someone

examples.text: Please answer the phone.

senses.definition: the part at the end of your leg that you stand on

examples.text: My left foot hurts.
We went to the park on foot.

senses.usageNote: Say 'on foot', not 'by foot' or 'by feet'.

senses.definition: the part of something that faces forward or is seen first

examples.text: Let's sit at the front of the bus.

translations.zh: 我们坐在公交车前面吧。

examples.text: There is a tree in front of our house.

senses.usageNote: 'In front of' means outside and before something. 'At the front of' means inside, in the first part.

senses.definition: to become a member of a group or club, or to do something together with others

examples.text: I want to join the swimming club.
Would you like to join us for lunch?

translations.zh: 你想和我们一起吃午饭吗？

senses.usageNote: 'Join' has no 'in' after it: 'join the team', not 'join in the team'. For an activity, 'take part in' is common.

senses.definition: a device you use to talk to someone who is far away

examples.text: My phone is in my bag.

senses.usageNote: Say 'on the phone': 'She's on the phone' (= talking on it). 'Phone someone' is common in British English.

senses.definition: to call someone using a phone

examples.text: I'll phone you tonight.

senses.definition: to have or use something together with other people

examples.text: I share a room with my brother.

translations.zh: 我和弟弟合住一个房间。

senses.definition: a board with words or a picture that gives information

examples.text: The sign says 'No parking'.

senses.definition: to write your name on something

examples.text: Please sign here.

senses.definition: one of the sides of a room or building

examples.text: There's a clock on the wall.

senses.definition: an opening with glass in a wall or car that lets in light

examples.text: Can you open the window, please?

senses.definition: to give something to someone in exchange for money

examples.text: They sold the shop last year.

senses.definition: very pleasant to look at or listen to

examples.text: What a beautiful view!

senses.definition: before now; in the past

examples.text: I moved here two years ago.

senses.usageNote: 'Ago' comes after the time: 'three days ago', not 'ago three days'. Use it with the past simple, not the present perfect.

senses.definition: to have the same idea as someone

examples.text: I agree with you.

senses.usageNote: 'Agree' is a verb, so say 'I agree', not 'I am agree'.

senses.definition: a very young child

examples.text: The baby is sleeping.

senses.definition: a period of one hundred years

examples.text: This house is a century old.

translations.zh: 这栋房子有一百年历史了。

senses.definition: to decide which one you want

examples.text: Choose a book you like.

senses.definition: having a low temperature

examples.text: It's very cold today.

senses.definition: a common illness that makes you sneeze and your nose run

examples.text: I've got a cold.

senses.definition: an electronic machine for storing information, writing and using the internet

examples.text: I do my homework on the computer.

senses.definition: with little or no light

examples.text: It gets dark early in winter.

senses.definition: close to black in colour

examples.text: He has dark hair.

senses.definition: a particular day of the month or year

examples.text: What's the date today?

senses.usageNote: Ask 'What's the date?' for the day of the month, and 'What day is it?' for Monday, Tuesday and so on.

senses.definition: to say what someone or something is like

examples.text: Can you describe your house?

translations.zh: 你能描述一下你的房子吗？

senses.usageNote: Do not add 'about': say 'describe the picture', not 'describe about the picture'.

senses.definition: to like doing or having something

examples.text: I enjoy reading comics.

senses.usageNote: After 'enjoy' use the -ing form: 'enjoy swimming', not 'enjoy to swim'. 'Enjoy yourself' means have a good time.

senses.definition: used to say that something is completely correct

examples.text: It's exactly three o'clock.

senses.definition: a story told with moving pictures that you watch at the cinema or on TV

examples.text: Let's watch a film tonight.

senses.usageNote: British English says 'film'; American English often says 'movie'.

senses.definition: after a long time; also used to introduce the last point

examples.text: The bus finally arrived.

senses.definition: in the place of someone or something else

examples.text: There's no tea. Would you like juice instead?
Let's walk instead of taking the bus.

translations.zh: 我们走路吧，不坐公交车了。

senses.definition: a child or young person

examples.text: The kids are playing in the park.

senses.usageNote: 'Kid' is informal. In writing, 'child' is more usual.

senses.definition: to pay attention to sounds or to what someone says

examples.text: I like listening to music.

senses.usageNote: Always use 'to' before an object: 'listen to the teacher', not 'listen the teacher'.

senses.definition: a person who is in charge of a shop, team or part of a company

examples.text: I'd like to speak to the manager.

senses.definition: the part or point that is at the centre

examples.text: There's a table in the middle of the room.

senses.definition: to be too late for a bus, train or plane

examples.text: Hurry or we'll miss the train.

translations.zh: 快点，不然我们就赶不上火车了。

senses.definition: to feel sad because someone is not with you

examples.text: I miss my grandparents.

senses.definition: plants, animals, the land and everything that people did not make

examples.text: I love walking in nature.

translations.zh: 我喜欢在大自然中散步。

senses.usageNote: No 'the' before 'nature' in this meaning: 'protect nature', not 'protect the nature'.

senses.definition: pleasant, good or kind

translations.zh: 好的；令人愉快的；友好的

examples.text: Have a nice day!

senses.definition: used when something is possible but not certain

examples.text: Perhaps it will rain later.

senses.definition: something you give to someone, for example on their birthday

examples.text: Thank you for the lovely present!

senses.definition: prepared and able to do something or be used

examples.text: Dinner is ready!
Are you ready to go?

senses.definition: to get something that someone gives or sends you

examples.text: I received a letter from my aunt.

translations.zh: 我收到了姑姑的一封信。

senses.definition: to keep money so that you can use it later

examples.text: I'm saving for a new bike.

translations.zh: 我正在攒钱买新自行车。

senses.definition: to help someone or something get away from danger

examples.text: The doctor saved his life.

senses.definition: how big or small something is

examples.text: What size shoes do you wear?

senses.definition: a person's male child

examples.text: Their son is five years old.

senses.definition: feeling bad because you have done something wrong or because something bad happened

examples.text: I'm sorry I'm late.

senses.usageNote: 'Sorry?' with a rising voice is a polite way to ask someone to repeat something.

senses.definition: having a powerful body that can carry heavy things

examples.text: He's strong enough to lift the box.

translations.zh: 他力气大，能搬起这个箱子。

senses.definition: something you study at school, such as maths or history

examples.text: Maths is my favourite subject.

translations.zh: 数学是我最喜欢的科目。

senses.definition: a person trained to treat people who are ill

examples.text: You should see a doctor about that cough.

translations.zh: 你的咳嗽应该去看医生。

senses.definition: to stop doing something because it is complete

examples.text: Have you finished your homework?
The film finishes at nine.

senses.usageNote: Use '-ing' after 'finish': 'I finished reading', not 'I finished to read'.

senses.definition: an amount or part of something

examples.text: Would you like a piece of cake?

senses.usageNote: Use 'a piece of' to count uncountable nouns: a piece of paper, a piece of advice, a piece of news.

senses.definition: to make something clear by describing it

examples.text: Can you explain the rules to me?

translations.zh: 你能给我解释一下规则吗？

senses.usageNote: 'Explain something to someone'. Never 'explain me something'.

senses.definition: in a higher place than something

examples.text: There is a clock above the door.

senses.definition: a living thing that can move, such as a dog or a bird

examples.text: What is your favourite animal?

senses.definition: a piece of furniture that you sleep on

examples.text: It's time for bed.

senses.usageNote: Say 'go to bed' (no 'the') when you mean going to sleep.

senses.definition: having the colour of a clear sky

examples.text: The sky is blue today.

senses.definition: starting your life

examples.text: I was born in 2015.

senses.usageNote: Say 'I was born', not 'I born' or 'I am born'.

senses.definition: a boy or man who has the same parents as you

examples.text: I have one older brother.

senses.usageNote: English does not have separate words for older and younger brother; say 'older brother' or 'younger brother'.

senses.definition: in a way that is easy to see, hear or understand

examples.text: Please speak clearly.

senses.definition: a group of people who meet to do an activity together

examples.text: I joined the chess club.

senses.definition: a place where people study after they leave school

examples.text: My sister is at college.

senses.definition: red, blue, green and so on

examples.text: What colour is your bike?

translations.zh: 你的自行车是什么颜色的？

senses.usageNote: British spelling is 'colour'; American is 'color'.

senses.definition: not living any more

examples.text: The plant is dead because I forgot to water it.

translations.zh: 那盆植物死了，因为我忘了浇水。

senses.usageNote: 'Dead' is an adjective and 'die' is a verb: 'The fish is dead', 'The fish died'.

senses.definition: to plan and draw how something will look or work

examples.text: She designed her own dress.

senses.definition: to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it

examples.text: Drink some water after the game.

senses.definition: a liquid that you drink, or an amount of it

examples.text: Can I have a cold drink?

senses.definition: to go or come into a place

examples.text: Please knock before you enter.

senses.usageNote: Say 'enter the room', not 'enter into the room'.

senses.definition: more than usual, or more than others

examples.text: I love fruit, especially mangoes.

translations.zh: 我喜欢水果，尤其是芒果。

senses.definition: the part of the day between the afternoon and night

examples.text: We watch TV in the evening.

senses.definition: to not pass a test or exam, or to not do what you tried to do

examples.text: He failed his driving test twice.

translations.zh: 他驾照考试没通过两次。

examples.text: Don't worry if you fail at first.

translations.zh: 一开始失败了也别担心。

senses.usageNote: You 'fail a test' (no 'in'). The opposite is 'pass a test'.

senses.definition: well or healthy; also good enough or OK

examples.text: I'm fine, thank you.
Tomorrow is fine for me.

senses.definition: money you must pay because you broke a rule

examples.text: He had to pay a parking fine.

senses.definition: the flat surface you walk on inside a room

examples.text: The toys are on the floor.

senses.definition: all the rooms on one level of a building

examples.text: I live on the third floor.

senses.usageNote: In British English the 'ground floor' is at street level, and the 'first floor' is one above it.

senses.definition: having the colour of grass and leaves

examples.text: She has a green bag.

senses.definition: the thin threads that grow on your head

examples.text: She has long black hair.

senses.usageNote: 'Hair' on your head is uncountable: 'Her hair is long', not 'Her hairs are long'.

senses.definition: to touch something quickly and with force

examples.text: She hit the ball over the net.

senses.definition: a building where ill or hurt people are looked after by doctors and nurses

examples.text: My aunt works at the hospital.

senses.usageNote: British English often says 'in hospital' with no 'the' when someone is a patient.

senses.definition: the number 100

examples.text: There are a hundred students in our year.

translations.zh: 我们年级有一百个学生。

senses.usageNote: No '-s' after a number: 'two hundred people', not 'two hundreds people'.

senses.definition: a man from a royal family who rules a country

examples.text: The story is about a kind king.
